reasoning: A magic sequence requires x[i] (for i=0 to 5) to equal the number of occurrences of value i in [x[0],...,x[5]]. All x[i] must be integers in [0,5]: values <0 are invalid for counts; values=6 lead to contradiction (would require all entries equal some j<=5 but also equal 6); values>6 exceed sequence length. Thus, sum x[i] = 6 and sum i*x[i] = 6, which implies x[0] = sum_{k>=2} (k-1)*x[k]. All non-negative integer solutions satisfying these equations (enumerated by cases on x[5], x[4], x[3], x[2]) were checked: [4,1,0,0,0,1], [3,2,0,0,1,0], [4,0,1,0,1,0], [4,0,0,2,0,0], [2,3,0,1,0,0], [3,1,1,1,0,0], [0,6,0,0,0,0], [1,4,1,0,0,0], [2,2,2,0,0,0], [3,0,3,0,0,0]. None have value frequencies matching the x vector itself (e.g., [2,2,2,0,0,0] has three 0s and three 2s, not two each). No other solutions to the sums exist, so unsatisfiable.
